walkthrough: Find the grating spacing from 400 lines per millimetre: $d = \frac{1.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}}{400} = 2.5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
State the condition for an intensity maximum at normal incidence: $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$, where $n = 0, 1, 2, ...$ and $\lambda = 700 \text{ nm} = 7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
The highest order occurs at the largest angle with $\sin\theta = 1$, so $n_{max} = d/\lambda$.
Substitute values: $n_{max} = \frac{2.5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}}{7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}} = 3.57$, so only integer orders $n = 0, 1, 2, 3$ are possible.
Count maxima on both sides of the central maximum: $2 \times 3 + 1 = 7$ in total. This is option B.
